survivor_adjudication.ruling: Both published texts are wrong, and the executor's is wrong in the direction that matters. 'Not defence in depth' is refuted: on my run :67 never decides anything, and the ref-currency moves this suite builds are decided at :31 - proven, not argued. The reason text's premise is also false: a W06-01 fixture does invalidate an input ref between reads (W06-01-NEG-RECHECK-POLICY-MOVED-REFUSED), so 'no W06-01 fixture invalidates a Requirement or input ref between reads' is a fourth measured-false statement about a guard's reachability. Round 4's wording is closer but incomplete: it is defence in depth for every class it tested, yet not a redundancy - the accepted-dependency-STALE-REPORT class is one only :67 refuses. The survivor entry must therefore read, and the row in checkpoint.falsifiability_survivors and any new precision note must say: 'survived: no fixture reaches :67's error path; :31 is the deciding clause for the ref-currency moves the suite builds (probe: faulting :31 reddens W06-01-NEG-RECHECK-POLICY-MOVED-REFUSED, faulting :67 reddens nothing across 126 gate + 25 reuse/dependency rows + the native-coordinator chain); :67 remains strictly stronger than :31 for a STALE REPORT input bound to an accepted dependency whose contribution proof is in the bundle, a state no fixture in the repository constructs, so owning this clause needs that construction, not a claim about it.'
